answer: A mechanism that actually bites: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because mirror only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, ripple is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any kernel approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
